column1:
Where must workflows be defined and what key responsibility do they have that jobs and steps don't?
  • Location: Workflows must be defined at the repository level - they cannot exist outside a repository
  • Unique responsibility: Workflows define the triggers that start the automation process
  • Structure: Trigger configuration happens only at the workflow level

column1: What is the default execution behavior of jobs in a workflow
column2:
and what must you do if you want jobs to run sequentially?
  • Default behavior: Jobs run in parallel by default
  • Example: If you create 10 jobs without dependencies
column3:
all 10 will run simultaneously when triggered
  • For sequential execution: You must explicitly specify job dependencies to control the order
  • Key point: Each job runs on a separate virtual machine
column4: so there's no shared state between jobs github-actions jobs parallel-execution

column1: How do steps execute within a job
column2:
and what's the only way to achieve parallel step execution?
  • Default execution: Steps always run sequentially within a job
  • No exceptions: This sequential behavior cannot be changed within a single job
  • For parallel steps: You must place steps in different jobs and configure those jobs to run concurrently
  • Execution flow: If any step fails

column1: What happens when a step fails in a job
column2:
and how is this visually represented in GitHub's interface? When a step fails:
  • The failing step shows a red X
  • All subsequent steps in that job are skipped
  • Skipped steps show a gray dash
  • The entire job is marked as failed
Visual indicators:
  • 🟡 Yellow dot = queued/running
  • ✅ Green check = success
  • ❌ Red X = failed
  • ➖ Gray dash = skipped

What's the difference between "GitHub Actions" (the platform) and "a GitHub Action" (the code unit)? GitHub Actions (platform):
  • The entire CI/CD platform provided by GitHub
  • Includes workflows
column4:
etc.A GitHub Action (code unit):
  • A reusable piece of code that can be executed in a step
  • Often sourced from other repositories or GitHub Marketplace
  • Example: actions/checkout@v3
  • Alternative to writing raw shell commands
Workflow vs Action:
  • Workflow = A YAML file defining the entire automation pipeline
  • Action = A reusable component used within workflow steps

column1: Create a workflow example that demonstrates both successful and failed step execution
column2:
explaining the expected behavior. Example workflow:

name: error-handling-demo
on: push
jobs:
  success-job:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: This will succeed
        run: echo "Success!"
      - name: This will also run
        run: echo "Still running"

  failure-job:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: This will fail
        run: echo "About to fail" && exit 1
      - name: This will be skipped
        run: echo "Never reached"

Expected behavior:
  • success-job: Both steps execute and show green checks
  • failure-job: First step fails (red X)
column3:
second step is skipped (gray dash)
  • Both jobs run in parallel despite one failing
